sections.body: Investigations may be administrative, civil, criminal, regulatory, or driven by industry and contract obligations, and each context changes authority, disclosure, evidence, and preservation expectations. Confirm who authorized the investigation, involve legal and privacy stakeholders, define scope and need-to-know, and establish reporting and documentation that records the question, facts, decisions, limitations, and recipients. Do not let curiosity, an informal request, or a well-intentioned administrator expand the inquiry beyond its authority.
keyPoints: Authority and purpose determine which actions are lawful and defensible.
A report should distinguish observed facts, interpretations, limitations, and recommended action.
Preserve potentially relevant evidence before ordinary operations overwrite it.
sections.title: Establish authority, reporting, and scope

sections.body: Evidence handling records what was collected, by whom, when, where, how, and under whose control. Investigative techniques include scoping, interviews, timeline construction, log correlation, acquisition, preservation, analysis, and reporting; tools and tactics must be authorized, validated, and appropriate to the question. Protect the original, use validated acquisition methods, calculate integrity evidence where appropriate, and distinguish data, computer, network, and mobile-device artifacts and their collection conditions. Every transfer, access, storage condition, and analysis action should be attributable. A technically interesting artifact is not enough if its provenance, integrity, or collection authority cannot be explained.
keyPoints: Chain of custody is a documented continuity of control, not merely a hash value.
Choose tools and tactics that preserve the artifact type and record versions, settings, and limitations.
Investigators should analyze working copies when practical and protect originals.
sections.title: Use techniques and tools to preserve evidence and custody

summary: An investigation seeks defensible facts while protecting people, systems, evidence, and legal rights. The investigator must establish authority, preserve the scene and chain of custody, limit disclosure, and document actions so findings can withstand scrutiny.

assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

learningJob.plainExplanation: Before rebooting, preserve relevant volatile evidence under the appropriate authority and record each action. Authority permits and limits collection, while custody documents handling without creating collection authority.
